text:
maria: Quick sync — thinking about the autoscale contract between the reservation-adaptor and the pool operator. Goal: avoid double-accounting warmup credits while keeping a fast admit path.

ryan: +1. short question: do we keep admit() side-effect free? currently admit reserves tokens and may trigger prewarm.

kevin: I'd prefer admit to be idempotent and side-effect-free. Concrete: AdmitRequest -> predicts required_headroom, returns AdmitToken that encodes a soft-reservation. then separate ExecuteRequest consumes token and triggers prewarm if needed.

sara: This means admission controller only checks budget and SLA, not actually allocate GPU. How do we handle burst credits then?

maria: plan: token contains {tenant_id, token_id, headroom, ttl, burst_class}. Billing/ledger increments on issue. Pool operator honors token at grant time and charges actual compute on Execute.

devon: Concern: token stash could be hoarded and expire unused causing charge mismatch. Need metrics: tokens_issued, tokens_consumed, tokens_expired per-tenant.

ryan: Agree, add simple expirer with callbacks to refund burst credits when token expires. Also surface token_latency metric (time between admit and execute) for warmup tuning.

kevin: API sketch:
```
POST /admit {tenant, req_gpus, preferred_latency}
-> {admit_token, estimated_warmup_ms, soft_reserve:true}
POST /execute {admit_token}
-> {allocated_node, kv_cache_hint}
```

sara: Nice. What about fallback? If execute can't allocate, we should have auto-fallback to shared-hosted pool or a lower-fidelity quantized model.

maria: yes — operator does best-effort; if fails it returns ExecuteResponse with fallback=true and fallback_strategy enum. Also emit event so requestor can retry with a different model.

devon: Observability: traces linking admit->execute->allocation, and a counter for fallback_reason. We'll need a migration plan for existing operator.

ryan: Migration: phase 1 - admit token returned but operator ignores token (legacy behavior). phase 2 - operator enforces tokens and emits refund events. phase 3 - operator supports prewarm hints.

kevin: One more ops detail: limit token lifetime to short window (e.g., 30s) to limit hoarding. But allow tenant override for scheduled batch jobs.

sara: Ops-bot: deploy queued for branch autoscale-token-proto. ETA 20m :rocket:

maria: Thanks all — I'll write a short RFC update with API shapes and telemetry list. If anyone wants to add test cases for token expiry edge cases, ping me.

ryan: I'll add unit tests for refund path.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded: autoscale-token-proto -> staging :white_check_mark:
